description:
## Goal
Make recursive-group search telemetry report the same canonical per-product work across process hash seeds without changing pull behavior.

## Reproducer and evidence
While implementing fz-kdt.5, two separate `fz2 --telemetry-jsonl` processes compiling `fixtures2/00420_enum_take_drop_split.fz` produced equal canonical request, evaluation, settlement, displacement, publication, demand-cone, and population dimensions after excluding only the already-proven CallableConstruction cache-hit redistribution. They disagreed on recursive search work for canonical CallableConstruction products: `recursive_dependency_reach_visits` (for example 43 versus 40), `recursive_candidate_scans`, and `recursive_searches` (for example 6 versus 4).

This is distinct from fz-kdt.47: that ticket explicitly says the cache-hit divergence does not prove formula/product-set divergence and routes product-work causality elsewhere. The recursive-search counters observe traversal/scheduling work directly and are not cache-hit dimensions.

## Suspected boundary
The reach query stops as soon as it finds a target while traversing hash-backed dependency collections. The set of reached candidates may be semantic, but visits before the early exit are traversal-order work. Candidate/search counts may additionally expose order-dependent pending-group scheduling. Re-derive each dimension before changing code; do not sort merely to disguise work.

## Acceptance
- A focused seeded-order test proves which recursive-search dimensions are semantic sets versus actual traversal work.
- Canonical per-product recursive searches, candidates, reached candidates, dependency visits, and successful publication membership are reproducible across processes, or the public report explicitly represents the true distribution with a justified stable comparand.
- Pull settlement/publication behavior and backend programs do not change.
- fz-kdt.5 cross-process acceptance needs no exclusion beyond the proven CallableConstruction cache-hit key.
- Update performance instrumentation/fact-engine docs and run target fixture, causal, cross-process, and warning-free checks.

comments.text: TDD implementation ready for cold review (uncommitted). Red: focused five-node pending graph failed on legacy early-exit reach work with left=1/right=5. Design deletes the separate reachability gate and repeated per-candidate SCC walks; one Tarjan traversal includes the prospective current->dependency edge, so it simultaneously detects the cycle and returns its members. Across 32 fresh RandomState memos the report is exact: candidate_scans=5, reached_candidates=2, dependency_reach_visits=5; a naive exhaustive-per-candidate rewrite would cost 41 SCC visits plus a separate gate. Checks: pull tests 31/31; full lib 1587 passed/5 ignored; target fixture interp/run/build 9/9; fz2_cli causal cross-process pass; clippy all-targets -D warnings pass; git diff --check pass. fz-kdt.5 must retain its JSONL/causal wiring and rerun its three-fixture cross-process acceptance after applying this structural diff.

title: [BUG] Make recursive-group discovery work reproducible across process hash seeds
